limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses alginate hydrogels as a model confining microenvironment, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo ECM complexity.
MSC migration was examined only in the context of viscoelastic and plastic matrices; the role of the nuclear piston in purely elastic or degradable matrices was not explored.
The theoretical model simplifies the complex cellular and molecular processes and may not capture all regulatory mechanisms.
The study focuses on protease-independent migration; synergistic effects with protease-dependent mechanisms were not investigated.
Experiments were performed with a single MSC line (D1 MSCs); generalizability to primary MSCs or other cell types is not established.
Long-term effects of ion channel inhibition or knockdown on cell viability and function were not assessed.
The role of other mechanosensitive channels or ion transporters beyond NHE-1 and TRPV4 was not examined.
The study does not address how the nuclear piston mechanism is regulated in different stages of migration or in response to varying matrix stiffness.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
